From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T15:12:00Z
Subject: Procurement playbook & deployment decision confirmation

Alex — thanks again for a productive call earlier. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we can align the procurement path and pricing: 

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Outcome desired: serve inference for patient-facing summarization and internal search with strict latency for interactive workflows.
- Primary POC scope: 3 models (chat + embedding rerank), expected steady throughput ~200 qps with spiky peaks to 600 qps during batch jobs.
- Initial region: us-east (primary), with failover to us-west.

Stakeholder mapping (from call):
- Technical champion: Alex Prince (you) — evaluation lead
- Security lead: Samir Patel (we talked about SOC2 + KMS)
- Procurement contact: procurement team (procure@brightarc.com)
- Economic buyer: Dana Lee (CFO) — controls budget/commits

Clarifying questions we need answered to finalize pricing + SLA proposal: 
1) Latency SLO: you mentioned "fast interactive" — can you confirm target p95 generation latency for typical chat calls (milliseconds)? e.g., p95 <150ms or p95 <300ms?
2) Unit cost constraint: do you have a target unit cost (monthly committed spend or $/1M tokens) we should optimize toward for the CFO conversation?
3) Deployment preference: do you want Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) or Private (VPC/on-prem) for the initial contract window? You said data residency matters — confirm if us-east Dedicated with tenant isolation is acceptable.
4) Contract and procurement: does BrightArc require a PO + standard redlines, or do we need an enterprise SOW + additional security addenda?

Next steps from my side: I will send a compact procurement playbook and our SLA/pricing summary tomorrow for your procurement and legal review. If you can confirm the three items above (latency target, cost guardrails, deployment preference) we will produce an optioned quote (Dedicated reserve + Dedicated burst + Private alternative) for Dana & procurement.

Proposed short call with procurement/legal: Tue 10/27 or Wed 10/28, 10–11am ET — does that work?

Attachments: none on this message yet — will share the playbook and SLA in the follow-up.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Procurement playbook & deployment decision confirmation

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. A few concrete answers from our side (so you can draft the playbook and quote):

Stakeholders (confirmed):
- Economic buyer: Dana Lee (CFO) — dana.lee@brightarc.com (will review price/commits)
- Procurement: procure@brightarc.com (primary contact for PO & T&Cs)
- Security/Legal technical: Samir Patel (samir.p@brightarc.com) and LegalOps (legal@brightarc.com)
- Platform owner: me (Alex Prince) for day-to-day evaluation

Decision criteria and targets: 
- Latency: target p95 inference latency for chat flows <= 200ms in us-east under expected load. For embeddings/rerank batch jobs we can accept higher tails (p95 <= 800ms).
- Cost: CFO looking at committed spend with a top-level target: keep inference unit cost below ~$1,200 per 1M tokens equivalent across our 3-model mix — we realize this is coarse.
- Deployment mode: preference is Dedicated reserved capacity in us-east with tenant isolation and optional Private (VPC) if there are blocking security controls.
- Security must-haves: SOC 2 Type II, encryption at rest + in transit, KMS integration (we use AWS KMS), audit logs retained 1 year.
- SLA: request for a 99.9% uptime SLA and clear incident escalation path; also RTO/RPO expectations for region failover.

Procurement process notes:
- We typically require a standard PO and run contract reviews through LegalOps. If you can provide a sample SOW + playbook that lists required evidence for security questionnaires we will hand that to LegalOps and procurement.

Thanks — I can join the procurement call on Tue 10/27 10am ET. Samir will attend for the security checklist.

— Alex
Alex Prince
Head of Platform Engineering
BrightArc Health

Alex — attaching the procurement playbook and a compact SLA/pricing spreadsheet per your request. High level:

What we attached:
- procurement_playbook_v1.pdf (short playbook with steps: technical evaluation -> procurement & legal -> reserved capacity commit -> onboarding)
- redwood_sla_summary.xlsx (SLA tiers + price bands; sample commitment options: Dedicated-2 (baseline), Dedicated-2 + burst, and Private-VPC option)

Quick answers to the items you flagged:
- Latency: based on your described profile (chat p95 <=200ms target), our Dedicated-2 config in us-east has historically met p95 <200ms for models of similar size at ~200 qps steady with burst headroom. We included the assumed token length distributions and test profile in the pricing spreadsheet.
- Cost mapping: pricing sheet shows an example mapping that targets ~ $1,200 / 1M tokens equivalent for a 12-month 50% committed discount scenario; there are tradeoffs between reservation sizing and burst credits which are called out.
- Security: SOC2 Type II evidence link included; we support AWS KMS integration and 12-month audit log retention. Neha has prepared a one-page controls summary attached to the playbook.
- SLA: we included a sample 99.9% uptime SLA option and the incident escalation path (Support -> SE -> Account Exec -> Engineering Pager). We also call out region failover procedures and expected RTO for cross-region failover.

Next steps:
1) Procurement call with your LegalOps + procurement on Tue 2026-10-27 10:00am ET — confirm if this is locked.
2) If procurement confirms PO flow and Dana OKs the high-level pricing, we will prepare a formal SOW and term sheet for signature.
